name: God Helmet classic (Shiva): right chirp, then amygdala both sides, 60 min
origin: Persinger & Koren (Laurentian University) sensed-presence protocol; home version by Todd Murphy (Shiva God Helmet software)
summary: Murphy's Shiva version of the Persinger/Koren lab design: a modulated-40 Hz 'chirp' stepping around the four right temporal coils, then an abrupt switch to amygdala burst-firing over both sides. Murphy reports presence, elation, joy, inner imagery or feelings of love in phase 2 and says the lab design gave visions of God only to a small percentage; independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012).
notes: Phase 1 (30 min): the chirp on the four right coils only. Murphy expects it to be somewhat unpleasant for many people (fear; he says women seem more prone): if fear comes, press Skip to go to phase 2 at once (his software shows a flashing 'abort' button for this) and do not make it into an endurance contest. Phase 2 (30 min, abrupt switch): amygdala burst-firing on all eight coils, left side clockwise and right side counter-clockwise. If anger or irritability appears during or after phase 2, never reuse this session. Not for people prone to anxiety. Not for anyone with a psychiatric diagnosis or medication, epilepsy, migraine or brain injury, or on drugs; no other mind machines at the same time; stop on any distress. Murphy's software plays phase 1 '10% higher than the volume level you entered (25% by default)' and says never to set the volume above 82%, since a higher setting would run the session 'at a volume above 92%, where signal distortion can occur'; 82 + 10 = 92, so the step is ten percentage points: 35% against 25% at the default setting. Here phase 1 therefore runs at the session intensity (1.4 µT by default) and phase 2 at 0.71 of it (about 1 µT); at higher settings the vendor's step is relatively smaller (60% against 50% is 0.83). The page names 'the second phase' in its 82% warning although the boost is in the first; this file follows the boost as described. The 'modulated 40 Hz chirp' template is proprietary. Murphy relates it to the frequency-modulated Thomas pattern, so it is approximated by a decelerating sweep from 40 to 6 Hz (the range is a choice) in 3-ms points, 2.5 s on and 1.5 s off: the 837 points of Dixon & Persinger 2001 (who used 1-ms points) at the 3-ms points of Tiller & Persinger 2002, once every 4 s; the 40 Hz modulation itself is not reproduced. The amygdala 'burstx' template is proprietary; it is approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz): 230 points as in Ryczko & Persinger 2002 (who used 4-ms points, once every 3 s), here at the vendor's standard 3-ms points (0.69 s, close to the 'about 0.7 s' burst of Persinger et al. 2009), then the vendor's 4 s silence; this gives about 9 s of field per minute (the vendor states 9.6 s). Coil steps: the step time is unpublished. Murphy calls the rotation the fast motion of the God Helmet, 'several times per second', and says each cycle around the temporal lobes 'takes a fraction of a second', so 62.5 ms per coil (4 cycles per second on each side) is used. Directions follow Murphy's 'Over the left side, the direction is clockwise, and over the right, it's counter clockwise', each side seen from its own side, as his coil-numbered God Helmet animations show (right coils 1-2-3-4 and left coils 5-6-7-8 each step top, back, bottom, front) and as his animation of the Koren helmet's right side shows; so here both sides step top, back, bottom, front (C5-TP7-T9-FT7 and C6-TP8-T10-FT8), starting at the top coil, and the placement order is set so the app's per-side directions mean exactly this. An image caption added to the session list in 2021 says the right side cycles clockwise; the text and the animations are followed. The cross centred near T7/T8 is an inference from 'four coils over each temporal lobe, above and forward of the ears'. Persinger's own account of the lab design (2002, reproduced on Murphy's site) gives the frequency-modulated signal over the right temporal lobe 'for 15 [or 20] minutes', then burst-firing over both sides 'once every three or four seconds for the same length of time'; Murphy's software runs 'each phase 20 minutes' (40-min session) or 'each phase 30 minutes' (60-min session). This is the 60-min version (30 + 30 min, longer than the lab's phases); the 40-min version is murphy-gh-chirpr-amybi-40min. Revised after a re-check of Murphy's session pages (2026): rotation 4 cycles per second instead of 2, the phase-1 boost read as ten percentage points (phase 2 at 0.71 of phase 1 instead of 0.91, with the session default raised to 1.4 µT so that phase 2 stays near 1 µT), the rotation direction now backed by the vendor's animations, and the lab's 15-20-min phases noted. Still approximate: both signal templates, the coil sites and the step time.
setting: Darkness and acoustic silence (the lab used an acoustic chamber that was also a Faraday cage, and gauze plus a blindfold). Relax without meditating or falling asleep. Lab sessions ran mostly between midnight and 4 am during geomagnetic quiet. A helper can press Skip during phase 1 so you stay in the dark.
schedule: At most once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 6, then a 21-day break; do not mix with other Shiva or Shakti sessions in the same weeks (Murphy). Murphy advises using other sessions first. Murphy's Shiva pages allow 60-min sessions weekly or every two weeks; his Shakti pages say at most once every 3 weeks.
